title: Each token becomes a vector
note: text = subtitles; say = spelled for the voice. Numbers from brain3d/trace.json, films/qkv_data.json, experiments/logs.

blocks.text: Last section, Emma's question became tokens. But token 19361 means nothing on its own. So each token looks up its row in a table.
blocks.say: Last section, Emma's question became tokens. But token one nine three six one means nothing on its own. So each token looks up its row in a table.

blocks.text: Each row is a vector: 896 numbers. Here is battery. Here is Manchester. The model learned every one of these numbers in training.
blocks.say: Each row is a vector: eight hundred and ninety-six numbers. Here is battery. Here is Manchester. The model learned every one of these numbers in training.

blocks.text: Why so many? Because a vector is a position, in a space of meaning. Words that are used alike end up close together. Squash the 896 dimensions down to three, and you can see it.
blocks.say: Why so many? Because a vector is a position, in a space of meaning. Words that are used alike end up close together. Squash the eight hundred and ninety-six dimensions down to three, and you can see it.

blocks.text: The bike parts gather here. The cities, there. The days and months, over here.
blocks.say: The bike parts gather here. The cities, there. The days and months, over here.

blocks.text: Ask which words sit nearest to battery, and you get batteries, lithium, capacitor, charger. Nearest to Manchester: Liverpool, Nottingham, Leicester, Leeds.
blocks.say: Ask which words sit nearest to battery, and you get batteries, lithium, capacitor, charger. Nearest to Manchester: Liverpool, Nottingham, Leicester, Leeds.

blocks.text: So the strip of tiles is now a row of 100 columns, each one a point in meaning. Next, those columns start to talk to each other.
blocks.say: So the strip of tiles is now a row of one hundred columns, each one a point in meaning. Next, those columns start to talk to each other.
